title: Canonical affine zero-section comparison constructions
statement: Fix finite coefficient data P [def-pur-conventions] and level n+1. Let B be a separated finite-type base over k [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let X_c, p_c and z_c be its ordered affine tower, projection and zero section [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use the unit and ordered shifted Tate target W_c of [def-pur-affine-space-thom-map], built from the specified twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and supported tensor convention [def-pur-supported-cup]. The coordinate source sheaves and exact degree-zero pullback comparison are those of [def-pur-affine-space-coordinate-boundaries]; exact site comparison is fixed by [def-pur-finite-site-coordinates]. The canonical constant-pullback identification identifies W_c with the source of the ordered affine-space comparison [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], formed from the recorded line comparison [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Define gamma on the unit using its ordinary constant finite-Tor witness. Using exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], define b_c: Rz_c^! W_c -> A_B by applying Rz_c^! to gamma, the conjugate compact-support compositor for p_c z_c = id [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], and the inverse of the exceptional identity unit. At c=0 use that same identity-adjunction normalization. For arbitrary g:B' -> B, define g_c:X'_c -> X_c by pulling back constants and preserving coordinates; its zero-section square is Cartesian. Construct the factorwise Tate pullback isomorphism by the exact inverse image, tensor and Tate-line comparisons. These primitives are used with the canonical closed exchange [def-pur-supported-class-operations] in the supported base-change map of the purity theorem module. All data are fixed constructions, with no purity isomorphism chosen.
